chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do not buy the crop before it becomes ready (ears of grain). If you buy its root, there is no harm in that. Or if you buy a palm tree, you buy its root, and if there is no fruit in it, there is no harm in that.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible
key_terms.يُسَنْبِلْ: to form ears (of grain); to become ready for harvest

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying crops or trees before they bear fruit in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between buying crops in their raw state (gharar) and purchasing the established root or tree, thereby permitting the latter to avoid uncertainty in trade. This ruling, found in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, clarifies the permissibility of buying unfruitful palms, emphasizing that the absence of current fruit does not invalidate the sale of the tree itself. This principle safeguards commercial transactions from excessive ambiguity while allowing flexibility in agricultural commerce.
